newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off but shrug Dow fall on apathy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off but shrug Dow fall on apathy.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended down on Wednesday but managed to resist the drop on Wall Street and hold steady near midsession levels on lack of investor interest, analysts and dealers said.

"The market remained weak but stable. They didn't even notice the drop in interest rates. I think the market has yet to digest first quarter earnings," said Esteban Rojas, associate research chief at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended down 24.21 points, or 0.64 percent, at 3,774.02. Trading volume was unremarkable at 70.3 million shares.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average meanwhile plunged 139.67 points to 7,085.65.
"There was very little volume, that is why it hardly moved. I would hate to call it a sell-off or profit-taking, it was more like drifting," a floor trader said.

Traders said the market did not benefit from a fall of 134 basis points to 18.37 percent on bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at Tuesday night's primary auction of government securities. "The market took little notice of Cetes rate falls, just look at the real rate." a desk trader said.
"Dealers feel rates could rise again, especially after today's advance in U.S. long bond yields," he added.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 28/32 to yield 6.96 percent in late trade.
Rojas said the market was awaiting further economic developments.
"We were waiting for news. Inflation data (for April) are due on Thursday or Friday, and look like being mild," he said.
A Reuters survey MEX22 of Mexico City financial firms showed they expected the consumer price index to gain by 1.11 percent in April, compared to 1.24 percent in March.
Dealers said that Telmex L shares, which accounted for 14 percent of all shares traded, weighed most on the downside.
The telecoms stock fell 24 centavos to close at 16.34 pesos, in tandem with its ADRs, which ended off 1/2 at 41-1/4.

The Bancomer financial group reversed an early gain to close down eight centavos to 2.80 pesos on fears higher domestic rates could increase its banking division's past-due loans burden, traders said.
Bancomer accounted for seven percent of all shares traded during the session.
Traders said they were somewhat surprised to see debt-ridden holding company Grupo Sidek at the head of the percentage gainers' list, followed by its tourist arm, Situr.
Sidek gained six centavos to 36 centavos, while Situr closed up four centavos to 24 centavos.
"The stock is so cheap it only takes a centavo to move the price a lot in percentage terms, but there is no fundamental reason of which I know," a desk trader said.
"It is cheap and it does have intrinsic value, but no one has recommended it for years," he added.
On the broad market, 104 stocks changed hands, with 54 ending lower and 31 advancing.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
